Bio

I’m Cade Armstrong, a first-year doctoral student in Aerospace Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin, advised by Dr. Luke Peterson and Dr. Ufuk Topcu. My primary research interests include orbital mechanics, trajectory design and optimization, multi-agent systems, and game theory. Through my research, I aim to improve the efficiency of space missions via improved decision-making and optimized trajectories. Additionally, I am passionate about teaching and aspire to teach at the university level, mentoring future engineers.

I spent the majority of my undergraduate studies conducting research with Dr. David Fridovich-Keil and the Control and Learning for Autonomous Robotics (CLeAR) Lab at UT Austin. Primarily focused on multi-agent interactions, I learned the fundamentals of multi-agent control and optimization through the lense of dynamic game theory. During this time, I worked alongside Ryan J Park to develop a novel game formulation that models foresighted agent behavior and an algorithm for inferring agents’ level of foresight from online data.

After recieving my B.S. in Aerospace Engineering from UT Austin, I began working the Center for Space Research, where I worked on problems pertaining to the orbital analysis, estimation, and prediction of the GRACE-FO formation. Additionally, I created a simulation for GRACE-FO’s inter-satellite range readings and implemented error reduction methods for the subsequent data processing.

Interests

Outside of academics, I enjoy reading sci-fi fantasy books, listening to and discovering new music, playing soccer, and trying new restaurants. I try to stay curious about the world around me and enjoy learning about new topics!
